_comment: EdUHK best-of-pool SHAPE corrections (VLM-verified). The EdUHK weight-column scraper splits a single 'The best ONE subject of {A, B, C or D} (x1.5)' clause into separate dict keys; unify's generic parser can then mis-read it as MULTIPLE best_of pools plus a stray FLAT weight, which over-weights more than one subject. These corrections restore the true single combined pool (2026) and the true flat weighting (2025). Applied via _apply_weight_corrections BEFORE year_changes and the EdUHK 2026-basis mirror, so both the year-change diff and the mirrored scoring use the corrected shape. The 'Specified ApL subject(s)' placeholder is kept verbatim in the flat map — apply_apl_policy expands it to the real ApL subjects (from eduhk_apl_weights.json) at the end of the run, so it does NOT need enumerating here. Edit THIS file (not the unified JSON) when a cycle's PDF changes.
_verified: 2026-07-16 — 2026: 'The best one subject of Chinese History, Economics, Geography or History (x1.5)'; 2025: each of Chinese History/Economics/Geography/History (x1.5). Reported: a student with Chinese History 5 + Economics 4 wrongly got BOTH x1.5.

JS8013._note: BSocSc Sociology & Community Studies + BEd (Primary Humanities). 2026 rule = best ONE of {Chinese History, Economics, Geography, History} x1.5 + Specified ApL x1.5. Scraper split it into best_of [{Chinese History},{Geography,History}] and leaked Economics into the flat map.
